newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs ease after Utsumi remark on bond bubble.
newsitem.headline: JGBs ease after Utsumi remark on bond bubble.

text.p: Cash and futures JGBs eased on Tuesday afternoon after a remark by former senior Finance Ministry official Makoto Utsumi that JGBs are at a "bubble" level and do not reflect economic reality, traders said.
The key September contract was at 125.80 at 0416 GMT, down from 125.85 at the outset of the afternoon session. It closed at 125.88 on Monday.

Utsumi, a former vice finance minister for international affairs who is now a professor at Keio University in Tokyo, said JGBs are trading at "bubble" levels and prices are likely to undergo a downward correction.
Some traders said the Fund had already placed some 70 billion to 80 billion yen worth of bids for the four-year JGBs.
The MOF earlier said it was offering 400 billion yen in new four-year JGBs with a 1.4 percent coupon through a price-competitive auction.
